Sara —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We filled the questionnaire (see attached) and included an exported subprocessor table with data boundary notes. High-level answers to the asks below:

- Access to request/response payloads: only Redwood-hosted model inference infrastructure handles request/response payloads. For Hosted API customers, payloads are processed in-memory on the inference nodes; persisted logs exclude full request/response content and are encrypted. Our subprocessor entries identify which vendors receive telemetry vs. content.
- AWS services: EKS (inference farms), S3 (artifact storage, customer-configurable backups), RDS (internal metadata), and CloudWatch for monitoring. All storage at rest is encrypted (AWS KMS). Specific service-level details are in the subprocessor document.
- Dedicated isolation: Yes — our Redwood Private product supports VPC deployment and customer-managed keys. I’ve added a note on the questionnaire about Private deployment options and who to contact for a dedicated eval.

Attachments: Acme_Redwood_Vendor_Questionnaire_filled.xlsx, redwood_subprocessors_20270615.pdf (updated).

Let me know if you want to set a 30-min sync with David (our security lead) to walk through architecture.

Sara / Marissa — forwarding a couple of quick clarifications from engineering:

1) Logs and telemetry: we retain aggregated telemetry for 90 days by default; customers can request different retention for Dedicated/Private deployments. Raw request payloads are not retained in the analytics pipeline; they are only used transiently for inference and obfuscated in traces.

2) Third-party access: monitoring vendor (DatabandOps) receives host-level metrics and anonymized error traces only; they do NOT receive full request content. Backup storage provider has access to encrypted object metadata only; keys are managed via AWS KMS and Redwood does not share plaintext keys.

3) Subprocessor additions: if Acme requires explicit contractual flow-downs for certain subprocessors, we can add them to the MSA Exhibit and include tailored security addenda.

If helpful, I’m happy to do a 30-min technical walkthrough next week (available Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Thanks,
